extracted.intended_audience: communication and journalism scholars; media researchers; newsroom practitioners interested in audience metrics
extracted.subtask_short: audience feedback effects on news production
extracted.subtask_description: A literature-review synthesis describing how various forms of online audience feedback (clicks, comments, shares, surveys) shape newsroom decisions, story selection, and audience interpretations. Useful for researchers studying news selection, newsroom practice, and metrics-driven editorial change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Behavioral Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Clicks, page views, dwell time, scroll depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are behavioral measures of consumption that newsrooms routinely collect and use as signals of audience interest (e.g., most-reads, views). They can be compared to editorial prominence to study alignment between readers' preferences and front-page placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments, shares, likes, reactions on social platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualify audience sentiment and active engagement beyond raw consumption; used by editors to infer interest and resonance, and may influence promotion decisions and perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey/Panel Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience research, reader surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct solicitations of audience preferences and attitudes provide qualitative and quantitative information distinct from behavioral traces; these are sometimes used alongside platform metrics to inform editorial strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent Misalignment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Quantitative studies comparing most-reads or -views to a story's position of prominence on a variety of media outlets' homepages found gaps between what readers like to read and what journalists choose to showcase."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding: front-page prominence does not always reflect most-read lists; misalignment should be expected and treated as a structural pattern rather than noise when analyzing homepages as a signal of newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Direct Influence of Metrics on Placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite the availability of metrics, traditional news values still dominate front-page placement decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors do not simply promote highest-engagement stories to prime homepage positions; professional newsworthiness criteria continue to play a substantial role when selecting front-page items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Influence Through Topic Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors use metrics not to choose individual stories but to inform topic-level decisions (more health coverage if health stories perform well).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience metrics shape resource allocation and beat emphasis over time rather than immediate story-by-story front-page choices; use of metrics is more strategic and aggregated at topic level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft News More Affected than Hard News
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience metrics shift coverage of soft / lifestyle / entertainment more than political/serious news (echoes Welbers et al. 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of heterogeneity: engagement-driven changes concentrate in entertainment and lifestyle beats, whereas hard news and public-affairs journalism remain more insulated from click-driven selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Younger and Online-Only Reporters More Receptive
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsroom subcultures vary in their willingness to integrate metrics; younger reporters and digital-first outlets more responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational culture and reporter demographics mediate how metrics are used; research and interventions should account for intra-newsroom variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Pursuit Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters increasingly check whether topics will engage before pursuing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-pitch metric-checking is a production behavior: reporters may avoid or pursue stories based on expected engagement, affecting beat coverage and investigative horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline Optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: A/B testing for clickability (especially in digital-first outlets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines are iterated and tested to maximize clicks; this practice is a concrete mechanism by which engagement metrics shape the product, with implications for tone and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and Promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about social-media promotion, push-notification, and email newsletter inclusion driven by predicted engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial promotion strategies are increasingly guided by engagement forecasts; allocation of promotional slots functions as a lever to boost stories that are expected to perform well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iteration Within Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories updated mid-cycle based on early click-through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-time or rapid updates to running stories occur in response to early audience signals, affecting content, emphasis, and follow-up choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-Level Resource Allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Beats with high-performing stories receive more reporter time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics influence long-term newsroom resourcing: successful topics attract additional staff/time, which can change coverage balance across the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cascade and Bandwagon Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing other readers liked a story increases own engagement (popularity feeds popularity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Popularity signals (e.g., trending indicators, share counts) can produce social contagion in consumption; researchers should account for endogenous amplification when interpreting metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Tone Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative comments below stories shift readers' interpretations independent of article content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User comments exert interpretive influence on subsequent readers; comment moderation and presentation therefore affect audience perception beyond the article itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized feeds shift exposure away from front-page agenda toward individual preference clusters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform-driven personalization fragments exposure and can decouple individual consumption from a site's editorial homepage, complicating the use of homepages as representative signals of public attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Track System of News Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern news selection runs two tracks: traditional editorial values (Galtung & Ruge tradition) and audience-engagement signals; both contribute, but neither dominates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical framework: treat front-page editorial selection and engagement-driven practices as parallel logics that jointly shape what audiences encounter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misalignment is Structural, Not a Bug
rubrics_metrics.description: The gap between 'most read' and 'front page' reflects a deliberate editorial choice to maintain professional newsworthiness norms against pure popularity metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operationalizing newsworthiness, researchers should recognize that differences between popularity and editorial prominence are often intentional and normative rather than mere error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-Page Composition as Label of Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Front-page composition continues to express editorial newsworthiness: this validates using homepage placement as a label for 'newsworthiness' in research, separable from 'engagement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological note: homepage prominence can be used as an operational measure of editorial newsworthiness distinct from engagement-derived measures like views or shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicts Diverging Outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlets that prioritize click metrics will systematically diverge from outlets that maintain editorial filters; both axes can be operationalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative analyses should consider outlets' orientation along the engagement-editorial axis, as this predicts systematic differences in coverage and homepage composition.
